Adjusted view using the April 2022 Beige Book: Despite headline Q1 GDP edging down, most Districts reported ongoing expansion supported by solid consumer spending and strong manufacturing activity. Labor markets remained very tight with robust job gains and widespread worker shortages, fueling strong wage growth. Price pressures intensified across virtually all Districts, with higher energy and nonlabor input costs, supply-chain disruptions, and low inventories keeping upward pressure on output prices. The FOMC’s May 4 actions (50 bp hike to a 0.75–1.00% target range, higher administered rates, and the June start of balance-sheet runoff) underscore a hawkish stance aimed at bringing inflation back to 2% amid added uncertainty from the Russia-Ukraine war and China lockdowns. Importantly, the April SLOOS indicated banks generally eased standards for C&I and some consumer products and saw solid demand, suggesting credit availability was still supportive and not yet a near-term drag. Balancing strong demand and employment against elevated inflation and geopolitical/supply risks, the Beige Book moves sentiment slightly less negative than an FSR-only read.
